source_user: Advanced cluster case multi-node NCCL-41: A multi-node NCCL job hangs only at larger world sizes. Produce a falsifiable diagnosis and rollback plan. Variant 41 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: test rank mapping, interface selection, topology, NIC affinity, rendezvous, firewall and ports, timeout logs, communicator formation, reduced-world baselines, and network counters. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Treat the larger-world-size hang as an observed symptom, not proof of a root cause. Assume the exact workload, collective and message shapes, failing world size, placement, and software stack can be reproduced; record NCCL/CUDA/driver/framework/launcher/container versions, node/GPU/rank membership and order, topology, TP/PP/EP mapping, InfiniBand versus RoCE mode, NIC/NUMA affinity, selected interface, MTU/routing, rendezvous endpoint, firewall/port policy, timeout settings, and clock synchronization. Do not invent platform facts; redact sensitive endpoints.

Falsifiable hypothesis for variant 41: communicator formation or collective ordering diverges on one rank at the larger size. Hold software, placement, workload, message sizes, and timeouts constant. First capture per-rank logs with synchronized timestamps and the communicator phase, then binary-search world size and run matched controls that vary one factor at a time: rank mapping, explicit interface/NIC affinity, approved transport choice, or an isolated reachability test. Predict that the suspected factor changes the first failing rank/phase, timeout location, or link/retransmit/error counters; a no-change control weakens the hypothesis. Compare at least repeated successful and failing trials, with correctness, initialization/collective latency (ms), timeout/retry counts, GPU/NIC utilization, link errors/retransmits, and cleanup success; report medians and dispersion, not a single run.

Safety and rollback: use read-only diagnostics and least privilege first, never expose credentials, and obtain authorization before changing interfaces, routing, firewall rules, MTU, NCCL settings, or placement. Canary one disposable allocation, stop on new errors, incorrect collectives, broader hangs, or timeout-budget breach, and revert the exact prior configuration. If the canary fails or evidence is contradictory, restore the prior configuration, terminate the canary cleanly, and do not claim a fix. Evidence is required before root-cause or improvement claims.
